These storms brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, moderate to heavy rainfall, and lightning, causing notable damage to property, specifically crops.
episodes.170053: Disturbances moved through a persistent southwest flow aloft across the region, which continued to provide daily afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms. These storms, some of which were severe, brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, heavy localized rainfall, and lightning.
episodes.170119: During the afternoon of Tuesday, July 5th, a complex of thunderstorms moved from South Dakota, eastward along a stationary front that lied near the Iowa border. North of this front, several lines of thunderstorms developed and moved eastward across far southern Minnesota. Although a few damage reports were noted, the main hazard was the increasing threat of heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Two areas of thunderstorms from southern Minnesota, and northern Iowa merged into a large complex as it slowly progressed to the east-southeast. Rainfall totals in a 3 hour period ranged from two to locally five inches from near Blue Earth in Faribault County, east to Albert Lea. The heaviest occurred over Albert Lea, and between Wells and Kiester in eastern Faribault County.
episodes.170505: An upper level disturbance produced widespread showers and thunderstorms across central Ohio during the overnight hours.
episodes.170537: A surface low situated over northern New England continued to push northeastward throughout the day, dragging a frontal boundary with it. This boundary became east-west oriented and stalled across the northern Ohio Valley throughout the day, placing Kentucky and areas southward in a warm and humid (unstable) air mass. Showers and storms developed during the afternoon hours across portions of the southern Ohio Valley, eventually leading to a MCS which traveled southeastward and into the Jackson forecast area by the evening. Winds were the main concern with storms throughout the day, especially along the MCS. SPC included much of central and eastern Kentucky in a Slight Risk for severe storms with wind being the main threat. This came to fruition as storms ended up producing widespread wind damage across portions of the southeast Ohio Valley and Mid-Atlantic.
episodes.170584: A derecho swept across South Dakota and into Iowa on the evening of July 5th. This resulted in a swath of  wind gust from 50 to 65 plus mph resulting in a number of power outages, tree damage, and a few damaged structures. A brief tornado occurred near Estherville with minor damage. As the bowing thunderstorm complex reach central Iowa the gusts had dropped below severe criteria given the less favorable environment with decreased deep layer shear.
episodes.170608: An isolated but intense thunderstorm resulted in widespread wind damage in and near the City of Staunton during the afternoon hours. Later that evening, a brief supercell produced localized wind damage in Prince William County.
episodes.170656: Severe thunderstorms produced six short-lived tornadoes across northeast Weld and Morgan counties.  Two of those landspouts were rated as EF1.  In Weld County, the tornado downed several trees and power poles.  In Morgan County, some oak trees were shredded and a power pole was snapped.  Across Douglas, Elbert and northern Lincoln counties, severe thunderstorms produced large hail, from quarter to half dollar size.  Strong thunderstorm wind gusts to 60 mph were reported along highway 71, south of Limon.
episodes.170663: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.170681: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a frontal boundary moving into a warm and humid airmass that was in place across the Ohio Valley.

episodes.170683: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a frontal boundary moving into a warm and humid airmass that was in place across the Ohio Valley.
episodes.170826: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over east-central Campbell County and produced quarter sized hail south of Rozet.
episodes.170838: A few thunderstorms produced sporadic gale force winds near a stalled warm front.
episodes.170888: Outflow from a thunderstorm produced a 67 mph wind gust at the Powell Airport.
episodes.171046: A stationary front draped north of West Viginia led to several rounds of showers and storms between July 5th and 6th. Overnight clusters of activity diminished each morning, allowing for a brief window of reprieve. This allowed the atmosphere to recharge for renewed convection during the afternoon and evening time frame. These storms contributed to downed trees from damaging wind gusts and localized instances of flash flooding due to heavy downpours. Over an inch of rain fell within strong and mature storms on these two days.
episodes.171183: As a frontal boundary held position over the Great Lakes region, southeast Ohio remained susceptible to strong thunderstorms on July 6th. The first cluster of stroms passing through in the morning resulted in quarter size hail being observed near the town of Eagle Mills in Vinton County. Later that afternoon, a second round of storms became organized and brought with it damaging wind gusts, leading to two trees down across Lawrence County.
episodes.171187: The hot and humid afternoon of July 6th brought forth strong to severe thunderstorms as a cold front remained parked in close vicinity to the area. Damaging wind gusts associated with these storms resulted in several downed trees and power lines within the Flatwoods and Summit townships.
episodes.171270: Strong to severe thunderstorms erupted along a slow moving cold front over southern WI. Large hail, damaging winds, and flash flooding occurred. A lightning strike and subsequent fire caused significant damage to a home in Beloit.
episodes.171340: A few severe thunderstorms and areas of localized heavy rain impacted southern portions of South Central Nebraska from the evening of Tuesday the 5th into the early morning of Wednesday the 6th. Fairly weak west to southwesterly mid-upper level flow was in place across the region. Surface low pressure was set up over northwestern Kansas, with a warm front extending east across northern Kansas by early evening. Across western Kansas south of this warm front, significant afternoon heating occurred, resulting in temperatures climbing to over 100 degrees and promoting steep low to mid-level lapse rates. Around 5 PM CDT, isolated thunderstorms began to develop slightly to the south of the local area within northern Kansas, but remained on the weaker side due to MLCAPE values around 1000 J/kg and weak deeper layer shear. In the meantime, radar imagery and surface observations depicted a well-defined cold front/outflow boundary sinking south through the region during the afternoon and early evening hours, emanating from intense convection across South Dakota and far northern Nebraska. By approximately 6:30 PM CDT this boundary was oriented roughly along the Interstate 80 corridor. Through the early evening hours, that initial area of isolated thunderstorms over north central Kansas gradually increased a bit in coverage, while drifting north into portions southwestern portions of South Central Nebraska. This activity moved into an area of better instability, with value closer to 2000 J/kg, but only a marginal improvement in deep layer shear. Between 8-9 PM CDT, there was brief time where convection was enhanced, as it met up with that southward sinking surface cold front. These resultant stronger storms mainly affected Harlan and Phelps counties, dropping hail up to the size of golf balls and producing wind gusts upwards of 70 MPH. ||Outside of this brief period of severe weather, weaker thunderstorm activity continued through the rest of the evening and overnight hours, driven by convergence along the nose of an increased low-level jet. There were no additional reports of severe weather through the overnight hours, but a swath of heavy rain developed across areas just north of the Nebraska-Kansas state line. Radar estimates showed an area of two inches or more extending from northeastern Franklin County east through portions of Nuckolls and Thayer counties, with higher amounts mainly concentrated over the northern half of Webster County. The highest amount measured by a mesonet station was 4.76 inches, located five miles north of Inavale. Numerous social media reports of 3-6 inches were received from the Bladen and Campbell areas, but there were no ground-truth reports of impactful flooding.
episodes.171505: During the late morning and early afternoon hours on July 6th, scattered showers and thunderstorms along a stationary front across central Indiana intensified and moved southward. As these storms moved into southern Indiana, they strengthened further thanks to a highly unstable environment, with mixed-layer CAPE approaching 3000 J/kg. The storms, which were initially somewhat discrete, grew upscale as they approached the Ohio River, with cold pool mergers helping to organize new convection. Sufficient downdraft CAPE helped damaging winds reach the surface, with scattered wind damage reports being observed across southern Indiana.
episodes.171507: Multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms moved across Kentucky between July 6th and July 8th. The main focus for convection was areas along and just south of a quasi-stationary surface front, initially positioned from west to east across central Indiana on July 6th. Each afternoon, thunderstorms developed in the unstable airmass, gradually pushing south and east before dissipating quickly after loss of daytime heating. On July 6th, a broken line of strong-to-severe thunderstorms crossed the Ohio River from Indiana during the mid-afternoon hours. As the storms pushed across central Kentucky, downdraft CAPE of greater than 1200 J/kg helped damaging wind gusts reach the ground, and several wind damage reports were observed, mainly across north central Kentucky. On July 7th, lesser instability led to the development of garden-variety thunderstorms, with wind damage only being observed in a few of the strongest cells. Finally, on July 8th, clusters of strong and severe thunderstorms produced scattered wind damage across south central Kentucky, with flash flooding also being observed in Russell County due to repeated bursts of heavy rainfall.
episodes.171545: A complex of thunderstorms developed in South Dakota on the morning of July 5, 2022. These thunderstorms tracked across Iowa, reaching western Illinois late that evening as a broken line of thunderstorms which produced one report of minor wind damage in Knox County.
episodes.171596: In the afternoon of the 5th, a line of pop-up storms began forming in southwest Nebraska. As one of these pop-up cells began to decay, it produced a downdraft that caused a 50 pound metal lid to fly off of a 10 foot tall bin.
episodes.171613: A significant supercell produced very large and destructive hail larger than 4 inches in diameter across Sioux County during the late afternoon into the early evening hours on July 5th. Further south, another cluster of severe thunderstorms produced wind gusts in excess of 70 MPH near Sidney.
episodes.171829: A line of showers and thunderstorms tracked east across Iowa Tuesday afternoon and evening bringing damaging wind, occasional lightning, and heavy rain to eastern IA and northwest IL.  The strongest reported winds of 60-70 mph, occurred in Buchanan and Linn counties.  These winds brought down trees and powerlines as they moved through in the evening.||A brief tornado occurred during the evening hours just southeast of Fairbank in an open field. Another brief tornado occurred just west of Winthrop IA in an open field.  Since no visible damage was observed with either tornado, they were assigned an EF-U rating.  The NWS would like to thank Buchanan County Emergency Management for assistance with the storm survey.
episodes.171835: A line of showers and thunderstorms tracked east northwest Illinois Tuesday evening bringing damaging wind, occasional lightning, and heavy rain.  The strong thunderstorm winds gusts of 60 to 70 MPH were reported at several locations in northwest Illinois.  These winds brought down trees and powerlines as they moved through in the evening.||In addition, heavy rain occurred with the highest amounts over 1 inch common in Jo Daviess and Stephenson counties in IL.
episodes.171837: Two rounds of storms tracked across portions of  northwest IL on Monday bringing torrential rain, occasional lightning, and gusty winds.  The first round moved through late morning and early afternoon along Interstate 80 from  the Quad Cities, towards Princeton IL.  Rain amounts over 1 inch were common with some totals over 3 inches reported in Bureau county in IL.  This caused some localized flash flooding occurred with these storms.  The second round of storms developed after 7pm across northeast IA and southern WI.  These tracked southeast into northern IL with gusty winds and torrential rain reported.
episodes.171925: A line of storms moved across southwest Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening of July 5th. Some of these storms produced hail, with the largest reported being penny sized in Preston (Grant County).
episodes.171943: Thunderstorms over eastern Montana moved into western North Dakota during the late evening hours. One thunderstorm produced penny size hail in Williams County.
episodes.171951: Storms repeatedly moved across portions of northeast Iowa during the evening of July 5th. Radar estimates suggest between 3 and 4 inches of rain fell from these storms which resulted in some localized flash flooding. Rocks and other debris were pushed onto some roads near McGregor (Clayton County).
episodes.172095: During the afternoon hours on the 6th, isolated storms developed over Eastern Colorado and evolved into a line of storms that moved east into Northwest Kansas through the night. These storms produced wind gusts estimated up to 60 mph across Cheyenne County, Colorado along with up to penny sized hail and heavy rain up to 4.5 inches. The heaviest rainfall amounts were reported in the eastern half of Cheyenne County with reports of visibility as low as one-eight of a mile at times. The heavy rain also caused some road flooding on a county road southwest of Arapahoe, Colorado that lasted through the late morning hours on the 8th. No damage was reported from these storms.
episodes.172104: A surface boundary from Dodge City to Hays helped to initiate a few thunderstorms that had up to golf ball size hail. Shear was average but ample CAPE over 2500 J/kg existed. More storms moved out of NW Oklahoma.
episodes.172190: A broken line of storms formed across the Texas panhandle into northwest Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 6th, with one report of severe wind received.
episodes.172200: Thunderstorms developed in the afternoon over and near the higher terrain, with an initial risk of strong to severe storms in the Pikes Peak region. This risk then spread into the eastern plains along the Highway 50 corridor later in the evening, where large hail damaging wind gusts up to around 75 mph, localized flash flooding, and even a tornado occurred.
episodes.172239: An isolated supercell produced large hail up to two and half inches in diameter, and wind gusts to 80 mph across portions of Barton and Rice counties in central Kansas on July 6th, 2022.
episodes.172480: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.172494: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region.  There were a few reports of flooding and trees down across southwest Georgia.
episodes.172497: A combination of weak steering flow and tropical moisture resulted in a slow moving thunderstorm over Cook county which produced isolated flash flooding.
episodes.172544: A complex of thunderstorms moved southeast from Kentucky and moved across southwest Virginia and East Tennessee. The storms produced hail and wind damage across portions of the area during the late afternoon and evening.

episodes.172595: Strong diurnal heating along with dewpoints in the upper 60s to mid 70s contributed to a highly unstable airmass. Multiple clusters of thunderstorms formed in the afternoon, resulting in damaging winds across northwest North Carolina.
episodes.172596: Strong diurnal heating along with dewpoints in the upper 60s to mid 70s contributed to a highly unstable airmass. Multiple clusters of thunderstorms formed in the afternoon, resulting in damaging winds across southwest Virginia.

episodes.172766: A line of thunderstorms moved southeast across western North Carolina during the evening. Several of the embedded storms produced locally damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172771: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed and moved over upstate South Carolina during the evening. A couple of the storms produced locally damaging wind gusts.

Once the heavy rain began on the evening of July 5th, flooding begin in several locations across south central McHenry County.  Minor ponding of water was reported on Route 120 east of Woodstock.  Significant ponding of water was reported on Route 47 south of Route 176.  Several inches of standing water was reported on Route 23, three miles south of Marengo. The initial tornado damage consisted of uprooted trees and damaged fences,  just south of the intersection of Oriskany Drive and Almahurst Lane. Damage continued along the lake shore of the community lake. The tornado intensified as it crossed Belle Meade Farms Drive and eventually Three Chimneys Lane, where minor roof and siding damage occurred along with dozens of snapped and uprooted trees. The tornado then crossed Wards Corner Road where it snapped a few dozen hardwood trees and caused more fence and minor roof damage. Additional damage was found along Murle Lane,|Ironwood Drive, and Paxton Woods Drive.||Additional damage extended all the way to State Route 28, but this was determined to be from straight line winds. Damage noted in this stretch included hundreds of downed trees and some minor property damage, including siding loss to a home.

The tornado touched down along Blue Sky Drive where several barns were damaged and multiple trees were uprooted and snapped. Additional damage consisting of dozens of snapped and uprooted trees occurred just southeast of the Huntley Road and Goshen Road intersection.||As the tornado approached Goshen, it rapidly strengthened and grew to around 500 yards in width. The tornado crossed Main Street, just to the west of State Route 28, causing significant damage to a couple of businesses. An insurance agency completely lost its roof and several of the exterior walls collapsed. A woman inside the business was transported to the hospital with non-life threatening injuries. The large and strong tornado then crossed State Route 28, significantly damaging a fire station and causing complete roof loss to a brick business next door. Most of the exterior walls on|the business also collapsed. A firefighter at the fire station also suffered minor injuries. This was the strongest point in the tornado life cycle with winds estimated around 130 mph.||The tornado continued moving southeast along Goshen Road, snapping hundreds of trees and causing at least six more homes to completely lose their roofs. A couple of additional homes also had some failure of exterior walls. The tornado struck both the middle and high schools causing some roof and siding damage. The tornado continued moving to the southeast crossing Woodville Pike near its intersection with Manila Road. The tornado then crossed Moler Road where it completely destroyed a barn and downed dozens of trees. Based on aerial footage, the tornado likely lifted somewhere between Moler Road and Cedarville Road.

Hundreds of trees blew down around the City of Staunton. Although most of the damage was consistent with wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph, there was one spot in the unit block of Morris Mill Road that had significantly more severe damage. In this area, a few hundred yard swath of trees snapped; most were healthy pine trees, and virtually every tree was snapped in half, all laying in the same direction. Elsewhere, a tree blew down onto a car on Devon Road; multiple trees and power lines blew down on Aiken Street; a large tree limb punctured the roof of a home on Garland Drive; several large trees blew down on Selma Boulevard, including a few into a house; several large pine trees snapped on Stonewall Circle and Knollwood Drive; trees blew down on Blair Street; numerous trees blew down on Poplar Street and North Drive.
